description: PlumeRoute is a live emergency map and fire-history detective, built on NASA satellite data. Live: FIRMS fires and GIBS imagery show where smoke is now; SAM 3.1 measures the plume, a 1–6h trajectory forecast shows where it will be, and a smoke-aware route guides you around it — with an avoid/caution/safe verdict by text or voice. Trend: a burning-activity calendar and year-over-year chart on the harmonized MODIS+VIIRS archive (2000–today) answer 'is this normal?', verdict computed in code.
summary:
PlumeRoute tracks any dangerous smoke — wildfire, industrial, or accident — live and over time, built on NASA satellite data.

The harmonized fire data problem: MODIS (1km, 2000–present) and VIIRS (375m, 2012–present) both detect active fires, but you can't compare them directly. A single fire is 1 MODIS point but up to ~7 VIIRS points, so raw counts make it look like fire exploded after 2012 when really the sensor changed. Brightness temperature also saturates differently across sensors.

Our fix: we harmonize them into active fire cells — one 0.01° cell with a detection on a day = one fire-day — and use Fire Radiative Power (MW), never brightness temperature. That gives one comparable series across sensors.

Live: FIRMS fires and GIBS imagery show where smoke is now; SAM 3.1 measures the plume, a 1–6h trajectory forecast on 850 hPa winds shows where it will be, and a smoke-aware route guides you around it, with avoid/caution/safe verdicts by text or voice.

Trend: a fire calendar and yearly chart on the harmonized archive (Brazil and USA, 2016–2025 in this build) answer 'is this normal?', verdict computed in code with a significance test
